title: Data Observability: Freshness, Volume, Schema & Distribution
interviewAnswer: Data observability monitors pipeline outputs beyond job success: freshness, volume, schema, nulls, distribution and lineage. A pipeline can be green while silently producing wrong data.
keyPoints: Baseline distributions and contracts catch silent shifts.
Route alerts to owners with context/lineage.
why: Data Observability: Freshness, Volume, Schema & Distribution is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: Data observability monitors pipeline outputs beyond job success: freshness, volume, schema, nulls, distribution and lineage. A pipeline can be green while silently producing wrong data. Baseline distributions and contracts catch silent shifts. Route alerts to owners with context/lineage. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: An ETL job succeeds but daily row count drops 80% because an upstream filter changed.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Data Observability: Freshness, Volume, Schema & Distribution?
How would you validate or tune Data Observability: Freshness, Volume, Schema & Distribution?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
